items.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: we don’t try to improve on Bach. We try to play it the way it was in his time.

ctx.x: So it’s a niche within a niche that you’re working in.

Well I mean I think that the entire spectrum could be brought up. I think, to me in other words we still, we don’t try to improve on Bach. We try to play it the way it was in his time. So why don’t we do the same thing with King Oliver? But I think eventually that will happen. There were some people who did try to do repertory bands, not too successfully. But I think succeeding generations will rediscover the early jazz. Because it’s too good. It just isn’t going to go away.
I think it’s hard to reproduce if it’s being played by conservatory-trained musicians.
